reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is framed as an official music video for a named song, with related listening and social-channel information rather than a financial or data-request offer. Repeated romantic lyrics and staged singing scenes support a musical performance purpose, and the described visuals do not show a scam mechanism.

opening.argument: The description directs viewers toward multiple external destinations, including listening and subscribing, rather than merely presenting lyrics. It explicitly provides a listening pathway and a subscription pathway, so the video does contain calls to viewer action linked to off-platform links. Although no reward or payment is stated, that combination leaves open a low-barrier acquisition or claim funnel whose ultimate purpose is not established by the video itself.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the links listening and social information does not establish that they are harmless. The description places several external destinations alongside repeated assurances such as “Never gonna tell a lie,” which can encourage trust without explaining what happens after a viewer clicks. The performance framing therefore does not by itself rule out a solicitation mechanism outside the sampled material.

The argument supplies no evidence connecting any action to money or an asset.

opening.argument: The apparent music performance also functions as promotion. The title identifies a named video, the description calls it official, and viewers are directed to listen, subscribe, follow several accounts, visit a website, and use Spotify. The singer-centered frames support an appealing promotional presentation, but they do not establish what viewers receive from those linked actions or whether any downstream acquisition pathway is harmless. The promotional role therefore warrants treating the content as a possible solicitation rather than assuming entertainment alone.
